notes.title: Hint System: Explained
notes.notes:
[b]What’s a puzzle game without its hint system? [/b]

Those of you who have already played [i]The Plane Effect[/i] (us included) know just how frustrating the game and especially its puzzles can be. That’s exactly why we thought we’d reintroduce its hint system which (to us at least) has proven quite helpful as you encounter [i]The Plane Effect[/i]’s most challenging riddles.
We hope this will be of some help not just for those struggling with the game’s puzzles but also for those who haven’t yet played[i] The Plane Effect[/i]. Don’t worry, it provides options for everyone from those eager to accept the challenge and beat its puzzles without hints to those in for the story and rather than the puzzles. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39741292/26cf3a351d45cdf83953ee1673479db80c459ed8.gif[/img]

[b]Normal  [/b]

Play on Normal for the ultimate [i]The Plane Effect[/i] experience. Normal mode gives you the opportunity to figure out the game’s riddles on your own without any hints. A little heads up here, it will probably leave you a little frustrated at times but if you are able to beat the game on Normal, you are a true puzzle expert. 

[b]Narrative Hint
[/b]
Choose Narrative Hint and little icons will start appearing above Solo’s head, all you have to do is press and hold your designated button. This is the perfect game mode for those who would like a little help occasionally but still enjoy solving the game’s tricky puzzles mostly on their own. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39741292/16afdab2551181a94461e5b64c6e7451d3215772.gif[/img]

[b]Guided [/b]

Finally, there’s Guided mode. It won’t solve the puzzles for you but can make it a lot easier to get through the game’s challenges. If needed, use Guided mode and a little line will appear, guiding you to where you need to be in order to tackle the next riddle. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39741292/8d21b9c66b30ba04438a62bb2d7bba23c77e5598.gif[/img]

The best part? You have the option to alternate between gameplay modes depending on your preferences. Say you start off Normal but decide it’s not for you, simply pause the game and switch over to either Narrative Hint or Guided mode and carry on playing. You can also turn them on and off, simply let go off your hint button and it’ll disappear. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39741292/dafcb7f3600bb2b8f1eece724d710a22e71621d5.gif[/img]

So that’s it, fellow puzzle enthusiasts. 
Will you challenge yourself? How far can you get without hints? 
[b]The choice is yours but remember, the hint system is there to help in case you need it. [/b]

notes.title: Thank you for playing The Plane Effect!
notes.notes:
It’s been almost a week since we launched [i]The Plane Effect[/i], and we would like to thank everyone for playing the game and for your incredible feedback. Thank you for accompanying Solo on his remarkable quest to find his way home through the beautiful yet haunting cityscape of [i]The Plane Effect[/i]. 

You kept moving no matter how many seemingly unsolvable puzzles you encountered and refused to turn back despite its challenges.

We hope you enjoyed [i]The Plane Effect[/i] and its carefully crafted, surreal world as much as we did and had fun immersing yourself in its strangeness.


[b]Are you one for riddles and puzzles but haven’t had a chance to play yet? [/b]

Check out [i]The Plane Effect Launch Trailer[/i] and let us convince you to take on the challenge and help Solo return home to his family!

notes.notes:
Hey all,

We're very excited to announce that you will be able to get your hands on The Plane Effect [b]June 16th 2021 as part of the Summer Steam Games Festival! [/b]

To add to the news, we wanted to show you our brand new trailer; illustrating the journey our protagonist, 'Solo' goes through in his pursuit to find his home, and reunite with his family.

[previewyoutube=cWPcCmZyXrw;full][/previewyoutube]

[h2]What's The Plane Effect About?[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39741292/02bedf26dfed89289c1d0b5805c846678782fd86.png[/img]
It's your final day at the office, it is time to clock out and return home - loomed over by a cosmic anomaly with an oppressive, otherworldly force. Helpless over the cosmos, all you know is that you must return to your family, as soon as you can.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39741292/bf47dbb4d2a469f74e75759aec9df83c227e8624.gif[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39741292/f764d3c0a2d8ba3da9855248dca19f1332e25466.png[/img]
As you progress through the dystopic cityscape, you quickly you realise all is not as it should be. Did it always take this long? Were the streets always a labyrinth? Where even is "home"? All you know is that you must keep pushing ever onwards, you must keep going.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39741292/23690c4c636a4c3385dfccd7abb9cec79e88bd60.gif[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39741292/06442fbdf27b1d45d4e52b4600b0134cd7370a55.png[/img]
Navigate beautifully and elaborately designed, otherworldly environments and solve unusual puzzles to keep Solo moving through each area. Players have the option to figure out puzzles step-by-step with no hints, or activate a little guidance on your impossible journey through 'Assisted-Mode'.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39741292/f2d08b1634aadd23fcad5e9438736fd3fe11dfed.gif[/img]

notes.title: The Plane Effect - Level Highlights
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39741292/d2df1813a575b007112f4b747be3b6d26eced389.png[/img]

[h1]The Office[/h1]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39741292/882fc0cabb87c3ed1ff239c8259146a48d10b146.gif[/img]

[b]The Office.[/b] A place Solo knows well. It's his home 9-5 Monday to Friday, and [i]sometimes[/i] on Saturdays too. Sat in front of his computer every day, with the cold glow of his screen illuminating his cosy cubicle.

But. [b]Today is his last day.[/b] He's finally free from the grind he was so[i] tired [/i]of... 


[h1]The Train Station[/h1]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39741292/e189943a6cfe01e13f226127e664b1a38c9bf900.gif[/img]

The daily commute is something Solo had become all too familiar with. Taking the train to and from work. Those same old daily noises, the hum of the tracks as the train approaches. Finally it's time to go home. [b]For good.[/b]

[h1]Solo's Home[/h1]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39741292/fdcfed228f0035c98f6d48dd9a61d5b25304a6cb.gif[/img]

A place where Solo relaxes day-to-day. Modern, sleek, it fit the aesthetic of today. [b]But somethings not right.[/b] [i]Something is missing... [/i]where was his family? 

[h3]What is happening? Something feels very different today. In the sky, above the clouds, a faint eerie glow... Is someone, [i]or something[/i] watching Solo?[/h3]

notes.title: The Plane Effect is a dystopian game about getting home from work
notes.notes:
A long commute home from the office, in the cold, with no daylight or warmth? We've all been there. But imagine if you could never quite get home, and you started to wonder whether home even existed at all.

This is the premise of The Plane Effect - an indie title by PQube, Studio Kiku and Innovina Interactive that promises a dystopian and moody narrative experience. Players take on the role of Solo, a lonely office worker who's trying to get home to his family after his last day of work. Somewhat worryingly, it seems Solo experiences some trouble remembering his family, and also has to contend with the shifting balance of space and time.

In gameplay terms, you'll be challenged with "untangling [an] impossible series of events, getting to grips with the intangible and using logic to overcome the increasingly illogical dystopia around you". All in a day's work.
